EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a classic monosubstituted benzene Raman pattern: a very strong ring-breathing band at 1003 cm⁻¹, strong CH out-of-plane deformation near 708 cm⁻¹, and ring C=C stretch at 1604 cm⁻¹. Additional in-plane CH/aromatic modes at ~1032, 1116, 1159–1205, and ring deformation near 623 cm⁻¹ support a phenyl ring. The strong aliphatic C–H stretches at 2967/2905/2871 cm⁻¹ and CH bending near 1446–1468 are consistent with a tert-butyl substituent. No strong sulfone S=O bands (~1140/1300 cm⁻¹) are evident, disfavoring sulfone-containing candidates. Overall, tert-butylbenzene (candidate 1) best fits the observed aromatic and aliphatic features; CH stretch region aligns with GFQ-003.
